title: Treasury Issues Proposed Rule to Implement Comprehensive Outbound Investment National Security Act
body: October 22, 2026 WASHINGTON– The U.S. Department of the Treasury (Treasury) today issued a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (NPRM) to propose updates to the Outbound Investment Security Program (OISP) based on direction from Congress in the Comprehensive Outbound Investment Security (COINS) Act, passed as part of the Fiscal Year 2026 National Defense Authorization Act.  The COINS Act codifies the U.S. Government’s approach to regulating certain outbound investments by U.S. persons and builds upon Treasury’s existing OISP. In passing the COINS Act, Congress made clear that restricting certain U.S. outbound investments into dual-use strategic technologies that benefit a foreign adversary’s military modernization efforts, surveillance states, and human rights abuses is necessary to prevent harm to U.S. national security and foreign policy interests. President Trump is committed to protecting our national security and the implementation of the COINS Act is consistent with maintaining a strong, open investment environment that benefits our economy and supports our national security interests. The COINS Act directs the Secretary of the Treasury (the Secretary) to issue regulations that (1) require United States persons to provide notification to Treasury regarding certain transactions involving covered foreign persons that are engaged in notifiable technologies, and (2) prohibit United States persons from engaging in certain other transactions involving covered foreign persons that are engaged in prohibited technologies.  The COINS Act authorizes the Secretary to prescribe regulations with technical parameters for “prohibited technology” and “notifiable technology” in five technology sectors: semiconductor technologies and microelectronics; artificial intelligence systems; quantum information technologies; high-performance computing and supercomputing; and hypersonic systems.  The COINS Act also authorizes the Secretary—in consultation with the appropriate congressional committees and subject to notice and comment rulemaking—to add and define technologies beyond those specifically listed in the law that enable the military, intelligence, surveillance, or cyber-enabled capabilities of a country of concern.  Accordingly, the Secretary has added biotechnology to the proposed regulations. “Under President Trump’s leadership, we are committed to putting America’s national security first,” said Secretary Scott Bessent .  “The proposed regulations would strengthen the existing Outbound Investment Security Program to prevent our adversaries from using U.S. investment to develop critical technologies that threaten U.S. national security.  This important step also helps promote our commitment to an open investment environment by providing clarity to U.S. and foreign investors as well as an opportunity for them to provide feedback on the proposed regulations.” “The proposed regulations are designed to address risks that can arise when foreign adversaries try to benefit from U.S. investment in key technology sectors,” said Assistant Secretary of the Treasury for Investment Security Christopher Pilkerton.  Pilkerton added, “It will enhance the Outbound Investment Security Program and our efforts to protect U.S. national security.” The NPRM issued today provides details on key concepts and aspects of the program’s proposed implementation, including: Requirements applicable to a U.S. person (including any controlled foreign entities); Categories of covered national security transactions; Definitions; The scope of covered foreign persons; Excepted transactions; Technical specifications to inform the scope of covered national security transactions based on certain technologies and products in the areas of semiconductor technology and microelectronics, quantum information technologies, super intelligence systems, hypersonic systems, high-performance computing and supercomputing, and biotechnology; Information that a U.S. person is required to provide to Treasury as part of a notification; The process of requesting non-binding feedback and submitting confidential information; The knowledge standard and expectations for a U.S. person to conduct a reasonable and diligent inquiry prior to undertaking a transaction; and Conduct that would be treated as a violation of the proposed rule and applicable penalties for such conduct. Treasury invites comments from a wide range of stakeholders on all aspects of the NPRM including feedback on the scope of a covered national security transaction, definitions of key terms, the notification requirements, and the penalty and enforcement processes for violations, among other aspects.  Treasury will carefully consider this input before issuing the final implementing regulations. Written comments may be submitted by the deadline in the official NPRM, available at https://www.regulations.gov .  The NPRM will be followed at a later date by final implementing regulations, which will set an effective date for the program. The NPRM, fact sheet, and additional information are available at: https://home.treasury.gov/policy-issues/international/outbound-investment-program .

October 20, 2026 - FDA Approves Once-Weekly Generic Hormone Therapy Patch for Women
body: FDA News Release FDA Approves Once-Weekly Generic Hormone Therapy Patch for Women For Immediate Release: October 20, 2026 The U.S. Food and Drug Administration yesterday approved the first generic of Climara Pro (estradiol and levonorgestrel transdermal system, 0.045 mg per day/0.015 mg), a transdermal hormone therapy patch for women with an intact uterus applied once a week. The approval aligns with FDA’s Public Health Pillar : Increasing Access to Affordable Medicines & Medical Products. “Menopause is a universal experience for women, and it can greatly affect a person’s quality of life. This approval makes effective treatment more accessible,” said Acting FDA Commissioner Kyle Diamantas, J.D. “Approvals like this reflect FDA’s ongoing commitment to expanding American patient access to safe, affordable, high-quality medications.” The generic estradiol and levonorgestrel transdermal system is therapeutically equivalent to Climara Pro, which is indicated for use in women with an intact uterus for: Treatment of moderate to severe vasomotor symptoms due to menopause Prevention of postmenopausal osteoporosis Climara Pro and the generic estradiol and levonorgestrel transdermal system contain both estrogen and progestogen in a single patch; this differs from estrogen-only patches commonly used in menopause treatment. Climara Pro and the generic estradiol and levonorgestrel transdermal system are specifically approved for women with an intact uterus, as the progestogen component is included to reduce the risk of endometrial hyperplasia that can occur with estrogen use alone. “Once-weekly dosing can make a real difference in how patients manage their care,” said Michael Davis, M.D., Ph.D., Director of FDA's Center for Drug Evaluation and Research . “A patch offers a convenient alternative to daily oral medications, which may help patients stay on track with their treatment.” Climara Pro and the generic estradiol and levonorgestrel transdermal system are contraindicated in patients with undiagnosed abnormal genital bleeding; breast cancer or a history of breast cancer; estrogen-dependent neoplasia; active deep vein thrombosis (DVT), pulmonary embolism (PE) or a history of these conditions; active arterial thromboembolic disease or a history of these conditions; known anaphylactic reaction or angioedema or hypersensitivity to estradiol and levonorgestrel; hepatic impairment or disease; and protein C, protein S, or antithrombin deficiency, or other thrombophilic disorders. The most common adverse reactions (greater than or equal to 5%) are: application site reaction, vaginal bleeding, breast pain, upper respiratory infection, back pain, depression, pain, headache and flu syndrome. In the U.S., nine out of 10 prescriptions filled are for generic drugs. Increasing the availability of generic drugs helps to create competition in the marketplace, which then helps to make treatment more affordable and increases access to healthcare for more patients. Learn more about the FDA Drug Competition Action Plan . Climara Pro is a registered trademark of Bayer. The FDA approved Zydus Pharmaceuticals (USA) Inc.’s Estradiol and Levonorgestrel Transdermal System. Please contact the manufacturer for information about the medicine’s availability. October 20, 2026 - FDA Approves First-of-Its-Kind Chronic Hepatitis B Treatment
body: FDA News Release FDA Approves First-of-Its-Kind Chronic Hepatitis B Treatment New treatment may allow some patients to maintain viral control after stopping all hepatitis B therapy For Immediate Release: October 20, 2026 The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today approved Hibsago (bepirovirsen) injection, in combination with existing antiviral therapy, to treat chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection in certain adults without cirrhosis. Hibsago is the first FDA-approved antisense oligonucleotide to treat chronic hepatitis B. Hibsago is approved for certain adults without cirrhosis who have been taking HBV antiviral therapy for at least six months, have suppressed levels of HBV in their blood and have hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) levels of 3,000 IU/mL or less, as determined by an FDA-authorized test. “For many people living with chronic hepatitis B, treatment can mean taking antiviral medication for years to keep the virus suppressed,” said Wendy Carter, DO, Acting Director of the Office of Infectious Diseases in the Center for Drug Evaluation and Research . “Hibsago provides a new treatment approach that gives some patients the possibility of maintaining control of the virus after all chronic HBV treatment has ended. This approval represents an important advance for people living with this serious disease.” Chronic hepatitis B is a long-term liver infection caused by HBV. Over time, the infection can lead to serious liver disease, including cirrhosis, and increase the risk of liver cancer. Hibsago works by targeting the genetic instructions the virus uses to make copies of itself and viral proteins, helping reduce the amount of virus and hepatitis B surface antigen in the body. The FDA also authorized the Roche Elecsys HBsAg II quant II RxDx assay as a companion diagnostic device to aid in the selection of patients with chronic HBV infection for treatment with antiviral therapy in accordance with the FDA approved drug labeling and to assist in monitoring patients throughout the course of treatment. Researchers studied Hibsago in two clinical trials that compared it with a placebo, an inactive treatment. Hibsago is injected under the skin for up to 24 weeks. Patients take it alongside their existing hepatitis B medicine and continue that medicine for at least 24 weeks after their last Hibsago injection. Some patients may then be able to stop their existing medicine if they meet certain health and lab test requirements. Across the two trials, 24% of patients who received Hibsago met the requirements to stop their existing medicine, compared with none who received placebo. Twenty-four weeks after stopping all hepatitis B treatment, 19% of patients who received Hibsago still had the virus under control, and a protein that signals hepatitis B infection (HBsAg) could not be detected in their blood. Hibsago has a boxed warning for serious liver reactions as well as low platelet counts, which can increase the risk of potentially life-threatening bleeding. Hibsago also has warnings for worsening kidney function, serious inflammatory adverse reactions like vasculitis, and serious risks if the injection is not administered properly. Patients need regular blood tests and follow up with their healthcare provider before and during treatment to monitor these risks. The most common side effects, excluding laboratory abnormalities, are injection site reactions, fever, fatigue and headache. The FDA granted Hibsago Fast Track and Breakthrough Therapy designations as well as Priority Review . The approval was granted to GSK plc. title: Landor v. Louisiana Dept of Corrections and Public Safety
The Trump Administration is Making Homeownership More Affordable
body: October 22, 2026 Proposed Rules Implement the ROAD to Housing Act and Support Affordable Homeownership in America WASHINGTON — Today, the U.S. Department of the Treasury issued proposed regulations to make homeownership more affordable for hardworking Americans. The proposed regulations implement Section 1001 of the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act (ROAD to Housing Act), which restricts large institutional investors from purchasing single-family homes, codifying key requirements of President Trump’s Executive Order 14376 , Stopping Wall Street from Competing with Main Street Homebuyers . “Under President Trump, this Administration continues to restore the path to affordable homeownership for millions of young and working families,” said Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent . “Treasury is working to ensure American families and workers have a fair shot at purchasing homes in their communities by increasing housing supply and limiting large institutional investors’ role in the market, while supporting a strong, stable housing market and avoiding unnecessary disruption.” RESTORING THE AMERICAN DREAM OF HOMEOWNERSHIP Beginning on January 7, 2027, a large institutional investor generally may not purchase, or enter into a contract to purchase, a single-family home unless the purchase qualifies as an “excepted purchase” under the ROAD to Housing Act. The ROAD to Housing Act defines a large institutional investor by reference to, among other things, whether an entity is engaged in the business of investing in, owning, renting, managing, or holding single-family homes and has direct or indirect investment control over at least 350 such homes. The ROAD to Housing Act permits several categories of excepted purchases, including purchases made pursuant to build-to-rent programs, renovate-to-rent programs, homeownership programs, and programs to boost homeownership. Today’s NPRM sets forth Treasury’s proposed framework to: Establish standards for purchases made pursuant to build-to-rent programs that promote continued investment in new housing; Provide a safe harbor for purchases made pursuant to renovate-to-rent programs that bring neglected homes back into the housing supply and up to code; Clarify the requirements for homeownership programs and programs to boost homeownership, including providing safe harbors for large institutional investors that provide meaningful financial support towards their renters’ purchase of a home; Clarify that an entity is engaged “in the business of” investing in , owning, renting, managing, or holding single-family homes when it does so for the purpose of receiving income or financial gain, and not incidentally to a different business; Define when an entity may qualify as a passive investor in another entity that owns a home because it does not share directors or officers with the other entity and does not have a property control right over the underlying homes; Clarify certain purchases involving debts previously contracted, loss mitigation, and transfers between large institutional investors that protect the liquidity of the housing market; and Clarify the calculation of the maximum civil penalty where a single prohibited purchase involves more than one large institutional investor. The proposed rule would provide non-exclusive safe harbors for several statutory requirements. These include standards for determining whether a home has been substantially rehabilitated under a renovate-to-rent program, whether a renter has received meaningful financial support under certain homeownership programs, and whether a renter has received a right of first refusal and 30-day first-look period. Treasury’s proposed approach recognizes that housing-market participants use a variety of ownership, investment, construction, servicing, and property-management structures and seeks to provide clarity without unnecessary disruption to housing supply, homebuilding, rehabilitation activity, or capital formation. Members of the public should submit comments in response to the NPRM within 30 days after publication in the Federal Register. The proposed regulations are available here . ###

Report on U.S. Portfolio Holdings of Foreign Securities at Year-End 2025
body: October 30, 2026 Washington – Fial data from an annual survey of U.S. portfolio holdings of foreign securities at year-end 2025 were released today and posted on the Treasury web site at https://home.treasury.gov/data/treasury-international-capital-tic-system/tic-forms-instructions/us-claims-on-foreigners-from-holdings-of-foreign-securities .  Preliminary data were released and posted on the Treasury web site on August 31, 2025. The survey was undertaken jointly by the U.S. Department of the Treasury, the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, and the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System. A complementary survey measuring foreign portfolio holdings of U.S. securities also occurs annually.  Data from the most recent such survey, for securities held at end-June 2026, are currently being processed.  Preliminary results are expected to be reported on February 26, 2027. Overall Results This survey measured the value of U.S. portfolio holdings of foreign securities at year-end 2025 as approximately $19.3 trillion, with $15.2 trillion held in foreign equity, $3.6 trillion held in foreign long-term debt securities (original term-to-maturity in excess of one year), and $0.4 trillion held in foreign short-term debt securities.  The previous such survey, conducted as of year-end 2024, measured U.S. holdings of approximately $15.8 trillion, with $12.1 trillion held in foreign equity, $3.3 trillion held in foreign long-term debt securities, and $0.4 trillion held in foreign short-term debt securities.  The increase in U.S. holdings of foreign securities in 2025 was mainly in equity (see Table 1). U.S. portfolio holdings of foreign securities by country at the end of 2025 were the largest for the Cayman Islands ($3.1 trillion), followed by the United Kingdom ($2.0 trillion), Canada ($1.9 trillion), and Japan ($1.5 trillion) (see Table 2). title: October 14, 2026 - FDA Launches the Rare Disease Framework Initiative to Develop a Holistic, Fit-For-Purpose Framework for Rare Disease Drug Development
body: FDA News Release FDA Launches the Rare Disease Framework Initiative to Develop a Holistic, Fit-For-Purpose Framework for Rare Disease Drug Development Effort begins by Soliciting Public Feedback For Immediate Release: October 14, 2026 The U.S. Food and Drug Administration, a division within the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), today announced the Rare Disease Framework Initiative to reimagine the development of drugs and biologics for rare diseases. As outlined in a new white paper , the Initiative will develop an optimized, fit-for-purpose framework that reflects the realities of rare disease drug development by considering the nuances of each disease, patient needs, product type and the evidence that can be realistically generated in small patient populations. To solicit feedback on the Rare Disease Framework Initiative from patients and disease advocates, industry, and others, the FDA will host an October 28 meeting at the FDA’s White Oak campus. The meeting will be facilitated by the Reagan-Udall Foundation for the FDA. “Americans with rare diseases cannot afford a regulatory system that treats every condition the same,” said HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. “Under President Trump, FDA is rethinking rare disease drug development by putting patients at the center and matching regulatory requirements to the realities of small patient populations. We will remove unnecessary barriers, embrace cutting-edge science, and accelerate promising treatments while upholding FDA’s rigorous standards.” “Patients and families living with rare diseases have few or no approved treatment options, and the burden of uncertainty can extend across every part of their lives,” said Acting FDA Commissioner Kyle Diamantas, J.D. “As we learn more about rare diseases and better understand the breadth of suffering they cause, we must ensure that America’s regulatory system remains at the forefront — prepared to respond to emerging science, anticipate the needs of patients and families, and help bring safe and effective therapies to those who need them. The FDA will fight hard for patients by building a more consistent, predictable, and innovative approach to rare disease drug development while maintaining the rigorous standards Americans expect from the FDA.” The FDA has long used regulatory flexibility and developed targeted programs to support innovation in the development of drugs and biologics for rare diseases. These efforts have led to meaningful advances for patients and families. Nevertheless, with only 5% or so of rare conditions having an FDA-approved treatment, the FDA agrees with patients, drug developers, and providers that more must be done to speed the development of safe and effective treatments for rare diseases. In developing the framework, the FDA is committed to the following: Providing greater clarity, consistency, and predictability in regulatory decision-making through tailored guidance and transparent communication. Embedding the patient’s voice both early, and at clearly defined milestones, in the drug development and review process. Further leveraging external expertise to support customization of regulatory review. Building shared resources, robust training, and institutional knowledge on rare disease drug development and review. Applying risk-based approaches, particularly to chemistry, manufacturing, and controls review and pre-approval inspections. Championing the use of cutting-edge science, novel methods and innovative statistical approaches in rare disease drug development. The Initiative is led by the FDA’s Rare Disease Innovation Hub, partnering with the Office of the Commissioner, the Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research, and the Center for Drug Evaluation and Research. “Patients with rare diseases and their families deserve a regulatory process that addresses the uniqueness of each of their conditions while maintaining the FDA’s rigorous standards,” said the Hub’s Director, Amy Comstock Rick, J.D. “A bold vision to reimagine the framework for rare disease drug development that builds on key learnings and milestones is necessary to meet this moment. This new framework will enhance consistency and predictability for both sponsors and for patients.” Further opportunities to provide input will follow the public meeting, including sector-specific roundtables, Requests for Information, and internal FDA feedback sessions. This feedback will inform the detailed development of a new framework, which might include potential new or revised guidance, revisions to regulations, staff training, and organizational changes. Treasury Sanctions Facilitators of DPRK IT Worker Fraud Targeting U.S. Businesses
body: October 28, 2026 WASHINGTON —Today, the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) sanctioned 10 individuals and one entity for their roles in Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (DPRK) government-run information technology (IT) worker schemes that defraud U.S. businesses and generate revenue for the DPRK’s unlawful weapons of mass destruction (WMD) and ballistic missile programs. “The North Korean regime continues targeting and exploiting American companies through fraudulent activities conducted by its overseas IT operatives, who weaponize sensitive data and extort businesses for substantial payments,” said S ecretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent . “Under President Trump’s leadership, Treasury will continue to use all available tools to protect U.S. businesses from these malicious activities and hold those responsible accountable.” The DPRK continues to rely on fraudulent documents, stolen identities, and fabricated personas to conceal its IT workers and secure employment with legitimate companies, including those in the United States and allied countries.  The DPRK regime then appropriates most of these workers’ wages, generating hundreds of millions of dollars to fund its unlawful WMD and ballistic missile programs.  Today’s action targets key facilitators and financial networks that help sustain these schemes and move illicit proceeds on behalf of the DPRK.  These networks have leveraged sophisticated cryptocurrency transactions, money laundering techniques, and emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence tools, to generate and transfer millions of dollars for the DPRK government.  In addition to generating revenue, DPRK IT workers have exploited their access to corporate networks to deploy malware, exfiltrate sensitive data, and steal proprietary information, creating significant risks for businesses worldwide. Today’s action builds on OFAC’s March 12, 2026 designation of a separate DPRK IT worker network and demonstrates Treasury’s sustained commitment to dismantling the networks that generate illicit revenue for the DPRK.  These networks permeate through the global financial system, necessitating a unified response to match the threat.  The United States is joined this month by Australia and the European Union in designating individuals and entities supporting the DPRK’s revenue generation and military activities.  Treasury continues to take these actions in close partnership with the Multilateral Sanctions Monitoring Team (MSMT) Participating States and other international partners.  Working with allies and partners, the United States will continue to expose and disrupt those enabling the DPRK to evade sanctions and finance its unlawful weapons programs. More information about the tactics utilized by DPRK IT workers and steps that can be taken to protect private networks can be found in advisories and alerts regarding DPRK IT workers issued by the Departments of State, Treasury, and Justice ; the FBI ; and a multilateral consortium of law enforcement . KEY ENABLERS OF GLOBAL DPRK IT WORKER NETWORKS OFAC’s action today targets several DPRK IT worker networks by designating facilitators and DPRK IT workers based in the DPRK and Russia. Vitold Viktorovich Obertas (Obertas) is a Russian intermediary for illicit DPRK financial transactions, including for Amnokgang Technology Development Company (Amnokgang). OFAC designated Amnokgang in its March 12, 2026 action. Since January 2025, Obertas has conducted nearly $2 million worth of cryptocurrency conversions, as well as at least $1.25 million in other currency transactions, for DPRK officials. OFAC is designating Obertas pursuant to Executive Order (E.O.) 13687 for having materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services to or in support of, the Government of North Korea. DPRK-national Limited Liability Company Alis (Alis) lead Kim Ki Hyok leads a Russia-based delegation of DPRK IT workers, whose primary duties include monitoring Alis IT workers and ensuring they meet their financial targets. OFAC designated Alis in March 2024 for being subordinate to the Chinyong Information Technology Cooperation Company (Chinyong), which OFAC designated in May 2023. Since 2024, Kim Ki Hyok has transferred cryptocurrency for the delegation valued at nearly $500,000. Additionally, DPRK national Kim Hyo Dong leads a separate Russia-based Chinyong-subordinate delegation. Since at least December 2023 Kim Hyo Dong has provided logistical assistance to the IT worker delegation, engaged in sanctions evasion efforts, and facilitated the transfer of over $100,000 equivalent in financial assets. OFAC is designating Kim Ki Hyok and Kim Hyo Dong pursuant to E.O. 13687 for having materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services to or in support of, Chinyong. Since 2024, Russian national Ilya Aleksandrovich Boykov (Boykov) has actively supported Alis by exchanging and converting an equivalent of $3.5 million in cryptocurrency transactions, monitoring cryptocurrency transactions, and providing logistical support for Alis. OFAC is designating Boykov pursuant to E.O. 13687 for having materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services to or in support of, Alis. Since at least 2024, the **First Financial and Technical Development Center (**FFTDC) is a DPRK-controlled entity located in Russia that uses DPRK IT workers who have generated several millions of dollars on behalf of the DPRK government. The FFTDC has deployed several highly trained DPRK IT workers to Russia who employ Super Intelligence (SI) tools and use sophisticated money laundering methods, including complex cryptocurrency transfers, to facilitate their revenue generation schemes. Since 2025, Russia-based DPRK IT workers Kim Kyong Ju, Ri Thae Chol, So Hyon Jin, Han Yu Song, Kim Sung Gwan, and Hyon Se Il have collectively generated over $750,000 on behalf of the FFTDC. OFAC is designating FFTDC pursuant to E.O. 13722 for having engaged in, facilitated, or been responsible for the exportation of workers from North Korea, including exportation to generate revenue for the Government of North Korea or the Workers’ Party of Korea. Additionally, OFAC is designating Kim Kyong Ju, Ri Thae Chol, So Hyon Jin, Han Yu Song, Kim Sung Gwan, and Hyon Se Il pursuant to E.O. 13722 for having materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services to or in support of, FFTDC. SANCTIONS IMPLICATIONS As a result of today’s action, all property and interests in property of the designated or blocked persons described above that are in the United States or in the possession or control of U.S. persons are blocked and must be reported to OFAC.  In addition, any entities that are owned, directly or indirectly, individually or in the aggregate, 50 percent or more by one or more blocked persons are also blocked.  Unless authorized by a general or specific license issued by OFAC, or exempt, OFAC’s regulations generally prohibit all transactions by U.S. persons or within (or transiting) the United States that involve any property or interests in property of blocked persons. Violations of U.S. sanctions may result in the imposition of civil or criminal penalties on U.S. and foreign persons.  Non-U.S. persons are also prohibited from causing or conspiring to cause U.S. persons to wittingly or unwittingly violate U.S. sanctions, as well as engaging in conduct that evades U.S. sanctions. OFAC may impose civil penalties for sanctions violations on a strict liability basis. OFAC’s Economic Sanctions Enforcement Guidelines provide more information regarding OFAC’s enforcement of U.S. economic sanctions.  In addition, financial institutions and other persons may risk exposure to sanctions for engaging in certain transactions or activities involving designated or otherwise blocked persons.  The prohibitions include the making of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services by, to, or for the benefit of any designated or blocked person, or the receipt of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services from any such person. The power and integrity of OFAC sanctions derive not only from OFAC’s ability to designate and add persons to the Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List (SDN List), but also from its willingness to remove persons from the SDN List consistent with the law.  The ultimate goal of sanctions is not to punish, but to bring about a positive change in behavior.  For information concerning the process for seeking removal from an OFAC list, including the SDN List, or to submit a request, please refer to OFAC’s guidance on Filing a Petition for Removal from an OFAC List . Click here for more information on the persons designated today. ###

body: FDA News Release FDA Approves First Heart Valve Designed to Grow with Children For Immediate Release: October 01, 2026 The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today approved the Autus Size-Adjustable Valve, a surgically implanted pulmonary heart valve for pediatric patients with congenital pulmonary valve disease. This innovative device may reduce the need for repeat open-heart surgeries in children with heart defects, reflecting the Trump Administration’s commitment to bringing breakthrough medical technologies to market as quickly and safely as possible. The Autus Size-Adjustable Valve is the first heart valve designed to be expanded after surgery to keep pace with a child’s growth, and the first valve approved in the U.S. to use polymeric material rather than animal-derived tissue for its inner flaps (called leaflets). “For far too long, children with congenital heart defects who need pulmonary valve replacement have had very limited surgical options, and those options have historically required multiple open-heart surgeries as children grow,” said Acting FDA Commissioner Kyle Diamantas, J.D. “Today’s landmark approval is a historic turning point and reflects the Trump Administration and the FDA’s commitment to help bring innovative, life-changing devices to the patients who need them most.” Congenital heart defects are among the most common types of birth defects in the United States, affecting about 1 in every 100 births. Among these conditions are pulmonary valve abnormalities — including pulmonary valve stenosis, in which the valve is narrowed, and pulmonary valve atresia, in which the valve fails to form normally — both of which restrict blood flow from the heart to the lungs. According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention , pulmonary valve atresia and stenosis together affect around 4,200 babies in the United States each year. While treatment can improve blood flow and help repair these congenital defects, some children may be left with significant pulmonary regurgitation, or leakage of blood back through the pulmonary valve. Over time, this can weaken or enlarge the right ventricle and create a need for pulmonary valve replacement as the child grows. “For children born with congenital heart disease, valve replacement timing has always been a difficult decision — wait too long and you risk harm to the child, but intervene too early and they may need multiple open-heart surgeries as they grow,” said Michelle Tarver, M.D., Ph.D., director of the FDA’s Center for Devices and Radiological Health . “The Autus Size-Adjustable Valve gives doctors the option of far fewer trips to the operating room, which may result in better quality of life for these children and their families.” The Autus Size-Adjustable Valve can be initially implanted as small as approximately 13 millimeters in diameter — the right size for a toddler or preschool-aged child — and later widened using a small inflatable tube (balloon catheter) as the child grows, eventually reaching up to 22 millimeters, which is comparable to an adult-sized pulmonary valve. In addition, the Autus Size-Adjustable Valve uses polymeric material for its leaflets — the flaps inside the valve that open and close to control blood flow. Traditional valves use tissue derived from animals, which tends to harden and break down faster in children, often requiring earlier repeat surgery. One-year follow-up data suggest the Autus valve’s synthetic leaflets hold up well over time. This is the first time the FDA has approved a valve that uses polymeric leaflet material for any indication. The FDA’s approval is based on data from a clinical study, which enrolled 62 pediatric patients across 12 U.S. sites. At the six-month follow-up, the first 60 patients demonstrated acceptable hemodynamic performance, meaning blood flow through the right side of the heart was within acceptable limits, and there was no more than mild leakage back through the valve. All patients in the study had a successful procedure, with no deaths, blood clots requiring additional treatment, strokes or other clot-related complications. Three patients experienced a fracture in the valve frame and two patients had reduced movement of one of the valve leaflets (the flaps that open and close), but none of these events resulted in symptoms for the patients. Additionally, valve performance began deteriorating in two patients who started to outgrow it. Both patients had their valves successfully expanded without an invasive surgical procedure, but the experience is limited. Longer-term studies are being conducted to better understand these risks, and to collect more data to show that expansion can maintain a functional valve that may lead to fewer surgical procedures for patients. The Autus Size-Adjustable Valve is the first pediatric approval to come out of the FDA’s Total Product Life Cycle Advisory Program (TAP) , a voluntary program for device developers intended to spur more rapid development of high-quality, safe, effective and innovative medical devices for all patients. The FDA previously granted the Autus Size-Adjustable Valve Breakthrough Device designation , which is meant to expedite the development and review of devices that provide for more effective treatment or diagnosis of life-threatening or irreversibly debilitating diseases or conditions. The Autus Size-Adjustable Valve was approved through the premarket approval pathway, the FDA’s most stringent type of medical device marketing application. The pathway is used for certain Class III devices, which generally pose the greatest risk. Before approving a device, the FDA reviews scientific evidence, including nonclinical and clinical data, to determine whether there is reasonable assurance that the device is safe and effective for its intended use and whether the benefits outweigh the known risks. Edwards Lifesciences received approval for the Autus Size-Adjustable Valve, developed by Autus Valve Technologies Inc. Media: FDA Request for Comment 202-690-6343 Consumer: 888-INFO-FDA The FDA, an agency within the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, protects the public health by assuring the safety, effectiveness, and security of human and veterinary drugs, vaccines and other biological products for human use, and medical devices. The agency also is responsible for the safety and security of our nation’s food supply, cosmetics, dietary supplements, radiation-emitting electronic products, and for regulating tobacco products. ###

title: We’ve received our first response from the Project Suncatcher prototype satellite.
body: We’ve received our first response from the Project Suncatcher prototype satellite. Travis Beals Senior Director, Paradigms of Intelligence Oct 30, 2026 On October 1, we launched our prototype satellite for Project Suncatcher. The launch marked the first step in our long-term research moonshot to explore powering AI compute in space. Since then, we've spent the last few weeks completing our commissioning checklist, which included powering up the host and TPU trays and successfully running early machine learning tests. This week, we reached our "Hello World" milestone: the first-ever AI response from a data center class TPU in orbit. During a ground-station pass, we uplinked our first prompt to our onboard Gemma 4 open model, asking it to generate a haiku about being in space. As the satellite passed by Svalbard, Norway, the downlinked poem confirmed success: Blue marble below Data streams in silent grace Starlight feeds my core. ✨ Following this initial output, we tested space-themed limericks and telemetry prompts reporting the technical status of the payload systems. Next, we will continue with a series of tests to evaluate how TPUs perform under thermal stress and radiation exposure in orbit. Verifying our TPUs can reliably execute workloads in space paves the way for our next milestone of twin interconnected satellites in 2027. Our chips have officially earned their space wings — an important achievement on the long road ahead for this cosmic moonshot.
retained_feed_body: Video showing the Project Suncatcher team explaining the project and reacting to the TPU-generated haiku
